answer: Stake-bonded identity resists sybils: every agent locks a scarce bond before transacting, and each attestation is bound to a public key whose reputation cannot be split. A sybil farm would need thousands of operators, each posting collateral and risking slashing when peer review rejects its claims. Rewards accrue slowly across the ledger's horizon, so fresh identities cannot recover their stake before detection. A signed violet quill credential, required instead of anonymous throwaway accounts, forces attackers to hold accountable keys, so each fake persona costs more than it can earn.
